examples.ko: 공사장에서 큰 폭발음이 들려서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled by a loud explosion sound from the construction site.
When the fireworks began, booming sounds rang out one after another.
The baby burst into tears because of the loud bang.

examples.ko: 밤중에 폭발음 같은 소리가 나서 밖을 내다봤어요.
examples.en: I heard a sound like an explosion in the night and looked outside.

examples.ko: 영화 속 폭발음이 너무 커서 귀를 막았어요.
examples.en: The explosion sound in the movie was so loud that I covered my ears.
Residents who heard the blast evacuated quickly.

explain: '펑' 하는 소리를 설명하는 말이라서 뉴스, 사고 이야기, 영화 감상에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '펑 소리', '큰 소리'라고도 말해요. '폭발음이 들리다/울리다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: There was a smell of gas, and then an explosion sound.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 생겼다는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that a sound occurred.

phrases.en: The neighbors said they heard an explosion at dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고를 목격한 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in accounts of witnessing an accident.

phrases.en: Suddenly there was a bang, so I ran outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is more natural in everyday conversation.

explain_en: It describes a loud '펑' bang, so it comes up in news, accident stories and movie talk. In casual speech people also say '펑 소리' or '큰 소리'. It is used as '폭발음이 들리다' or '폭발음이 울리다'.

examples.en: Flames shot up from the building, so fire trucks were sent out.

examples.ko: 화염에 휩싸인 차에서 사람들이 겨우 빠져나왔어요.
examples.en: People barely escaped from the car engulfed in flames.
The whole mountain was covered in flames.

examples.ko: 소방관들이 화염 속으로 들어가 사람을 구했어요.
examples.en: Firefighters went into the blaze and rescued a person.
They say they came down the stairs to escape the flames.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 화염과 연기가 가득한 장면을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a scene full of flames and smoke on the news.

explain: '불'보다 크고 거세게 타오르는 불길을 말할 때 써서 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '불'이나 '불길'이라고 해요. '화염에 휩싸이다'가 자주 쓰는 짝이에요.

phrases.en: The warehouse was engulfed in flames in an instant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불길이 크게 덮친 모습을 말할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for being swallowed by big flames.

phrases.example: 거센 화염 때문에 소방관이 가까이 가지 못했어요.
phrases.en: The firefighters couldn't get close because of the fierce flames.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세게 타오르는 불길을 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express strongly burning fire.

phrases.example: 화염 속에서 아이를 구한 소방관이 화제예요.
phrases.en: The firefighter who rescued a child from the blaze is in the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불길 한가운데를 말하는 표현으로, 뉴스나 이야기 글에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the middle of the fire; used in news and narrative writing.

explain_en: Written or news style for intense flames in a fire scene. It is used for big, fierce flames and shows up in news and writing. In everyday talk people simply say '불' or '불길'. A common pairing is '화염에 휩싸이다' (be engulfed in flames).

t90.ax: The whole mountain was covered in flames.

examples.en: When the wind blew, the dust rose up like a whirlwind.
A water whirl formed over the sea.
The fallen leaves spun around in a spiral shape.
A whirlwind blew and my umbrella flipped inside out.

examples.ko: 아이가 회오리에 휘말린 먼지를 신기하게 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: The child watched in wonder at the dust caught in the whirl.
The whirl disappeared quickly, but everyone was startled.

explain: 바람이나 물이 빙빙 돌며 올라가는 모양이에요. 바람 이야기에서는 '회오리바람'이라고 자주 말하고, 물이나 마음속 혼란에는 '소용돌이'를 더 많이 써요. 큰 혼란을 비유할 때도 쓰여요.

phrases.example: 그 발표는 업계에 큰 회오리를 몰고 왔어요.
phrases.en: That announcement stirred up a huge upheaval in the industry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 사회나 집단에 큰 혼란과 변화를 일으킬 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when something causes major turmoil and change in a society or group.

explain_en: It describes wind or water spinning around and rising. For wind people often say '회오리바람', and for water or emotional turmoil '소용돌이' is more common. It is also used figuratively for big upheaval.

en: to rage; to sweep; to drive

examples.en: Last night a fierce blizzard raged all night.
A strong wind is sweeping across the seaside.
A typhoon is raging, so the ships can't sail.

examples.ko: 슬픔이 휘몰아치는 바람에 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: Sorrow surged over me, so I couldn't say a word.

examples.ko: 소나기가 휘몰아칠 때는 밖에 나가지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't go outside when a downpour is sweeping in.
Suddenly a rainstorm started lashing outside the window.

explain: 바람, 눈, 비가 세게 한 방향으로 몰려올 때 써요. 감정이나 사건이 한꺼번에 밀려오는 느낌에도 쓰는데, 이때는 '슬픔이 휘몰아치다'처럼 주어가 감정이에요. '불다'보다 훨씬 거칠고 기세가 센 느낌이라 가벼운 바람에는 어울리지 않아요.

phrases.en: On typhoon days, wind and rain lash fiercely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨가 아주 거칠 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing for very rough weather.

phrases.example: 휘몰아치는 파도를 보니까 바다에 들어가기 무서웠어요.
phrases.en: Seeing the raging waves, I was afraid to go into the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '휘몰아치는 + 명사'로 거센 기세를 꾸며 줄 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The 휘몰아치는 + noun form conveys a fierce force.

phrases.en: Listening to the breakup song, my emotions surged.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음속 감정이 한꺼번에 밀려올 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor for emotions flooding in all at once.

explain_en: Use it when wind, snow or rain comes rushing in hard. It also describes emotions or events that surge in all at once, with the feeling as the subject, as in '슬픔이 휘몰아치다'. It sounds much rougher and more forceful than '불다', so it doesn't fit a gentle breeze.

examples.en: The air-raid siren suddenly sounded, so everyone took shelter.
Hearing the air-raid siren in the movie was scary.
We stayed underground until the air-raid warning was lifted.

examples.ko: 이 도시에서는 매달 공습경보 훈련을 해요.
examples.en: In this city, they hold an air-raid drill every month.
The news reported that an air-raid warning had been issued.
Where should I go when I hear an air-raid siren?

explain: '공습경보가 울리다', '공습경보를 발령하다', '공습경보가 해제되다'처럼 짝이 되는 동사가 정해져 있어요. 뉴스나 훈련 안내에서 많이 나오는 말이에요. 같은 경보라도 불이 났을 때는 '화재경보'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The air-raid siren sounded loudly during the drill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 나는 것을 말할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for the siren sounding.

phrases.en: The government issued an air-raid warning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이 공식적으로 알릴 때 써서 뉴스에 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an authority officially issues it; common in news.

phrases.en: The air-raid warning was lifted an hour later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험이 끝나서 경보가 풀렸다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the danger has passed and the warning ended.

explain_en: It pairs with set verbs, such as '공습경보가 울리다', '공습경보를 발령하다' and '공습경보가 해제되다'. It appears often in the news and drill announcements. For a fire, the matching alarm is called '화재경보'.

en: bolt from the blue; sudden disaster

examples.ko: 갑자기 회사가 문을 닫는다니 이게 무슨 날벼락이에요?
examples.en: The company is suddenly closing? What a bolt from the blue!

examples.ko: 선생님이 꼼꼼하셔서 숙제를 안 내면 날벼락이 떨어져요.
examples.en: My teacher is meticulous, so if you skip homework you get a real scolding.

examples.ko: 시험 전날 갑자기 날벼락 같은 소식을 들었어요.
examples.en: The day before the exam I suddenly heard shocking news.
Walking down the street, I felt as if I had been struck by lightning.
The layoff notice hit our family like a bolt from the blue.

examples.ko: 엄마의 날벼락 같은 목소리에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled by my mom's thunderous voice.

explain: 원래는 맑은 날 갑자기 치는 벼락이지만, 지금은 예상 못 한 나쁜 일이나 갑작스러운 큰 꾸중을 말할 때 더 많이 써요. '날벼락이 떨어지다', '날벼락을 맞다'로 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: Out of nowhere, the exam was suddenly canceled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전혀 예상하지 못한 일이 갑자기 일어났을 때 써요. 주로 나쁜 일에 쓰지만 놀란 감정을 강조하기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something completely unexpected happens suddenly, mostly bad news, to stress the shock.

explain_en: Originally it is lightning striking suddenly on a clear day, but now it is often used for an unexpected bad event or a sudden harsh scolding. It commonly appears as '날벼락이 떨어지다' or '날벼락을 맞다'.

en: to invade; to trespass; to break in

examples.en: A thief broke into the house at night.
The enemy troops cross the border and invade.
Someone tried to break into my computer.
Bugs got into my room and I was startled.
The person who sneaked in was caught by the police.

examples.ko: 창문으로 침입할 수 있으니 꼭 잠가요.
examples.en: Someone could get in through the window, so be sure to lock it.

explain: '침입하다'는 허락 없이 들어간다는 나쁜 느낌이 강해요. 그냥 들어가는 건 '들어가다'예요. 나라나 땅에 크게 쳐들어가는 건 '침략하다'를 쓰고, 이쪽은 전쟁 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: An intruder came into the house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허락 없이 들어온 사람을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word for a person who entered without permission.

phrases.en: A thief broke in through the window and stole money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들어가서 이어서 한 일을 말할 때 연결해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Link it this way to say what was done after breaking in.

phrases.en: Someone sneaked in and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday expression with a similar meaning.

explain_en: Illegal entry into a house or place, like a burglar. 침입하다 carries a strong sense of entering without permission, which is bad. Simply going in is 들어가다. For attacking a country or land on a large scale, use 침략하다, which has a war feeling.

t90.ax: A thief broke into the house at night.

examples.ko: 국회가 싸움 때문에 파행을 거듭하고 있어요.
examples.en: The National Assembly keeps being disrupted because of infighting.

examples.ko: 회의가 파행으로 끝나서 아무것도 결정하지 못했어요.
examples.en: The meeting ended in disarray, and nothing was decided.
The event ran in a disrupted way because of a sudden blackout.
Criticism poured in that the event was badly run.
I'm worried the class will be disrupted.
As the disruption dragged on, citizens' complaints grew.

explain: 뉴스에서 회의, 국회, 수업, 행사 운영이 제대로 돌아가지 않을 때 써요. '파행을 겪다/거듭하다/빚다'처럼 말하고, 반대 상황은 '정상 운영'이에요.

phrases.en: The meeting ran into disruption because of the conflict.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운영이 제대로 안 되는 일을 당했다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that operations went wrong and ran into trouble.

phrases.example: 국회가 파행을 거듭해서 법안이 처리되지 않았어요.
phrases.en: The National Assembly kept being disrupted, so the bill wasn't handled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 되풀이될 때 쓰는 뉴스 투의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news-style phrase used when problems keep repeating.

phrases.example: 교사가 부족해서 학교가 파행 운영을 하고 있어요.
phrases.en: The school is running irregularly because of a shortage of teachers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정상적이지 않게 운영된다는 뜻으로, 기사에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being run abnormally; often used in news articles.

explain_en: The news uses it when meetings, the legislature, classes or events fail to run properly. It goes like '파행을 겪다/거듭하다/빚다', and the opposite situation is '정상 운영' (normal operation).

examples.en: These days fake news runs rampant on the internet.
I hate a world where lies run rampant.
They say thieves were everywhere in the old days.
Illegal ads are everywhere in every alley.

examples.ko: 거리에 쓰레기가 판치지 않게 같이 치워요.
examples.en: Let's clean up together so trash doesn't take over the street.
If rip-off prices run rampant, tourists decrease.

explain: 주로 좋지 않은 것이 마구 퍼져서 세력을 떨칠 때 써요. 좋은 일에는 잘 안 쓰고, 비슷한 말로 '활개 치다'가 있어요. '판쳐요/판치는'처럼 활용해요.

phrases.en: It's a society where fraud runs rampant.
phrases.nuance_ko: '판치다'와 같은 뜻이고, 띄어 써서 '판을 치다'라고도 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 판치다, also said in the spaced form 판을 치다.

phrases.en: Bad rumors are running wild.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋지 않은 것이 거리낌 없이 퍼질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something bad spreads without restraint.

phrases.example: 가짜 물건이 판치지 못하게 막아야 해요.
phrases.en: We have to stop fake goods from running rampant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 나쁜 것이 퍼지지 않게 한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form means preventing something bad from spreading.

explain_en: It is mostly used when something bad spreads widely and takes over, so it does not fit good things. A similar expression is '활개 치다'. Conjugations are '판쳐요' and '판치는'.

en: to throb; to palpitate; to beat

examples.en: My heart always pounds before an interview.
My heart raced the night before the trip.

examples.ko: 그 사람을 보면 두근두근하는 마음을 숨길 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't hide how my heart pounds when I see him.

examples.ko: 내일 결과를 기다릴 때도 가슴이 두근두근할 거예요.
examples.en: My heart will be pounding tomorrow too while I wait for the results.
My heart was pounding and my hands got sweaty.
My heart is racing, so I can't sleep.

explain: '가슴이 두근두근하다'처럼 주어는 보통 '가슴'이나 '마음'이에요. '두근거리다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 설렘과 긴장 둘 다 되지만, 무서워서 뛸 때는 '쿵쾅거리다'나 '떨리다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: My heart is pounding, so I can't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두근두근하다와 같은 뜻이고, 일상 대화에서 더 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 두근두근하다 and heard more often in daily talk.

phrases.en: I opened the letter with a pounding heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -는 lets it describe the noun that follows.

phrases.en: My heart races when I see the person I like.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두근두근하다와 비슷하지만 더 짧고 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 두근두근하다 but shorter and more basic.

explain_en: Heart beating from excitement or nervousness (시험 결과를 기다리는 동안 계속 가슴이 두근두근해요.) The subject is usually 가슴 (chest) or 마음 (heart), as in 가슴이 두근두근하다. 두근거리다 means the same. It covers both excitement and nerves; for fear, 쿵쾅거리다 or 떨리다 sounds more natural.

t90.ax: My heart is racing, so I can't sleep.

en: fiercely; with a sudden outburst; angrily

examples.en: The child suddenly screamed at the top of his voice.
He got angry and snapped back fiercely.
My younger sister cried, screaming her lungs out.
No matter how I coax him, he just keeps insisting fiercely.

examples.ko: 엄마한테 바락 화를 내고 나서 후회했어요.
examples.en: I lashed out at my mom and then regretted it.
It felt so unfair that I shouted out before I knew it.

explain: 갑자기 크게 소리 지르거나 대들 때 쓰는 말이에요. '바락 소리를 지르다, 바락 대들다, 바락 악을 쓰다'처럼 말해요. 같은 말을 반복한 '바락바락'도 써요.

phrases.example: 동생이 갑자기 바락 소리를 질러서 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling suddenly shouted, and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 크게 소리칠 때 가장 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for suddenly shouting loudly.

phrases.en: The child talked back fiercely to the mother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화가 나서 윗사람에게 거세게 맞서는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes angrily talking back to someone, especially an elder.

phrases.example: 그는 바락바락 악을 쓰며 화를 냈어요.
phrases.en: He yelled at the top of his lungs in anger.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바락'을 반복해서 소리를 계속 지르는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The repeated form for shouting again and again.

explain_en: Spoken; suddenly raising one's voice in anger (바락 소리를 지르다) It describes suddenly shouting or lashing out. Typical phrases are '바락 소리를 지르다', '바락 대들다' and '바락 악을 쓰다'. The repeated form '바락바락' is also used.

en: to be startled; to flinch in fright

examples.en: The door suddenly opened and I was startled.
I flinched when I heard a noise behind me on the night road.
My sibling woke from a dream and sat up with a start.

examples.ko: 그는 전화벨 소리에 소스라쳐서 컵을 떨어뜨렸어요.
examples.en: He was so startled by the phone ringing that he dropped his cup.
I almost jumped out of my skin when I saw a snake at my feet.
My friend flinched as if startled.

explain: 주로 '소스라치게 놀라다' 꼴로 써요. '깜짝 놀라다'보다 몸이 움찔할 만큼 크게 놀랄 때 어울려요. 활용은 소스라쳐요, 소스라쳤어요예요.

phrases.example: 갑자기 큰 소리가 나서 소스라치게 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: A loud noise came suddenly and I was badly startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소스라치다'를 가장 자주 쓰는 꼴로, 몸이 움찔할 만큼 크게 놀랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form of 소스라치다, used when you are startled enough to flinch.

phrases.en: I was startled by the thunder and woke up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀란 이유를 이어서 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form used to link the reason for being startled.

phrases.en: The lights suddenly went out and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소스라치다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 소스라치다 and more common in everyday speech.

explain_en: It is mostly used in the form '소스라치게 놀라다'. Compared with '깜짝 놀라다', it fits a shock big enough to make your body flinch. The conjugations are 소스라쳐요 and 소스라쳤어요.

t90.ax: My friend flinched as if startled.

examples.ko: 동생이 장난감을 못 사게 되자 심통이 났어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling got sulky when he couldn't get the toy.
Why is your little brother acting spiteful since this morning?
My older brother is so cranky that we often fight.
He is sitting there with a sulky face.

examples.ko: 괜히 심통 부리지 말고 말로 해요.
examples.en: Don't throw a tantrum for nothing, just say it in words.
He acted spiteful and ended up getting scolded.

explain: '심통이 나다'는 마음에 안 들어 기분이 상했을 때, '심통을 부리다'는 일부러 투정이나 못된 짓을 할 때 써요. 아이나 가까운 사이에 잘 어울리고, '심술'과 비슷한 짝으로 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: My little brother is being spiteful today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '심통'과 비슷한 말이고 짝으로 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A close word to 심통 that often pairs with it.

phrases.en: He is sitting there with a sulky face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기분이 상해서 뚱한 표정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a sulky, displeased expression.

phrases.en: Please don't act mean to your friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 못되게 구는 사람에게 그만하라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone to stop being deliberately mean.

explain_en: Temporary sulking, grumpiness (심통이 나다); spoken, often playful. '심통이 나다' is used when you are upset because something is not to your liking, and '심통을 부리다' when you deliberately act spiteful or throw a fit. It suits children or close relationships, and often pairs much like '심술'.

examples.ko: 그는 학벌에 대한 열등의식이 있다고 해요.
examples.en: They say he has a sense of inferiority about his educational background.

examples.ko: 열등의식은 남과 비교할 때 더 커져요.
examples.en: A sense of inferiority grows bigger when you compare yourself with others.
I started working out to get free of my sense of inferiority.

examples.ko: 열등의식 때문에 사람들 앞에서 말하기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: Because of my feelings of inferiority, it's hard to speak in front of people.

examples.ko: 아이에게 열등의식을 심어 주면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't plant a sense of inferiority in a child.

examples.ko: 열등의식도 잘 쓰면 노력하는 힘이 돼요.
examples.en: Even a sense of inferiority can become a driving force if used well.

explain: 일상에서는 '열등감'이 더 자주 들리고, 열등의식은 설명하거나 글로 쓸 때 어울려요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '우월감'이에요. '콤플렉스가 있다'도 비슷한 뜻으로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I feel inferior when I compare myself to my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 남보다 못하다고 느낄 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when one feels inferior to others.
phrases.en_equiv: to feel a sense of inferiority

phrases.en: He suffered from a sense of inferiority for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 마음 때문에 오래 힘들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when that feeling troubles someone for a long time.
phrases.en_equiv: to be tormented by a sense of inferiority

phrases.en: I lack confidence because of my feelings of inferiority.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '열등의식'보다 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common than 열등의식 in everyday conversation.

explain_en: Formal/psychological — settled mindset of being inferior (친구는 어릴 때부터 열등의식 때문에 많이 힘들어했어요.) In everyday speech '열등감' is heard more often; 열등의식 suits explanations and writing. The opposite feeling is '우월감'. Koreans also say '콤플렉스가 있다' with a similar meaning.
